explication:
<explanation>
1. Identify the project type and purpose  
   - This is a large, open-source, cloud-native CLI toolkit (written in Go) called “SlimToolkit” (formerly DockerSlim).  
   - Its purpose is to inspect, profile, optimize, debug and secure container images (Docker and Kubernetes), generating smaller, more secure images and auto‐generated Seccomp/AppArmor profiles.  

2. Main architectural components  
   a. CLI Front-End (cmd/slim)  
     - Entry point: `slim` binary (interactive prompt via go-prompt)  
     - Dispatches user commands (`xray`, `build`, `debug`, etc.) to the Master Controller  
   b. Sensor Agent (cmd/slim-sensor & pkg/sensor)  
     - Embedded in temporary containers for dynamic analysis  
     - Implements monitors (fanotify, ptrace, HTTP crawler, etc.)  
     - Reports file-system events, syscalls and application behavior back to Master via IPC (Docker volumes or direct Docker API copy)  
   c. Master Controller (pkg/app/master)  
     - Orchestrates static image analysis (pkg/docker/dockerfile, pkg/docker/dockerimage, pkg/imagereader)  
     - Orchestrates dynamic analysis (spawns containers with sensor, collects artifacts)  
     - Builds application artifact graph (pkg/appbom, pkg/report)  
     - Generates optimized Dockerfiles, Seccomp/AppArmor profiles (pkg/app/master/compose, pkg/app/master/security)  
     - Invokes image builder (pkg/imagebuilder) or Docker build via go-dockerclient  
   d. Docker & Kubernetes Adapters (pkg/docker/dockerclient, pkg/app/master/kubernetes)  
     - Interfaces with Docker Engine (via go-dockerclient) or Kubernetes API to pull/start/push images and run containers  
   e. Image Builder Engines (pkg/imagebuilder/internalbuilder | external Docker)  
     - Internal: builds optimized images without Docker  
     - External: invokes Docker or alternative builders  
   f. Reporting & CLI Output (pkg/report, pkg/app/master/command/<cmd>/handler.go)  
     - Produces CLI logs, JSON reports, interactive tables, screencasts  

3. Relationships & data flows  
   - User → CLI Front-End (commands)  
   - CLI Front-End → Master Controller (command dispatch)  
   - Master Controller → Docker/K8s Adapter (API calls to pull/run containers)  
   - Master Controller → Sensor Agent (inject sensor into temporary container → start application)  
   - Sensor Agent → IPC channel (writes event logs, artifacts to volume)  
   - Master Controller ← IPC channel (reads dynamic analysis artifacts)  
   - Master Controller → Static Analyzers (layer diff, Dockerfile reverse-engineering)  
   - Master Controller → Image Builder (new Dockerfile + artifacts)  
   - Image Builder → Docker/K8s Adapter (build/push optimized image)  
   - Master Controller → Reporting (CLI/JSON/seccomp/AppArmor profiles)  

4. Architectural patterns & principles  
   - Modular, package-oriented design: clear separation of CLI, controller, adapters, sensor, analyzers, builders  
   - Command pattern: each subcommand is a handler plugged into a central dispatcher  
   - Adapter pattern: abstracts Docker vs. Kubernetes runtimes  
   - Producer-consumer: sensor produces events, master consumes them  
   - Layered architecture: CLI → Controller → Service/Analyzer → Adapters → External runtimes/services  

5. Key technologies, frameworks & libraries  
   - Language: Go  
   - CLI: c-bata/go-prompt, cobra-style command handlers  
   - Docker API: fsouza/go-dockerclient  
   - Kubernetes API: client-go abstractions in pkg/app/master/kubernetes  
   - Dynamic monitors: madmo/fanotify, ptrace, kernel interfaces (pkg/sensor/monitor)  
   - Static analysis: compose-go, dockerfile-ast, Go AST & file-diff logic  
   - Testing: BATS for acceptance tests, Go unit tests, end-to-end stubs  
   - CI/CD: GitHub Actions, Gitpod, Makefile, Docker, scripts directory  

6. Tailoring your system-design diagram for this open-source tool  
   - Emphasize the core CLI & Controller as the “brain”  
   - Show the Sensor Agent as a side-car process inside target containers with an IPC channel back to Master  
   - Distinguish static analyzers (layer diff, Dockerfile reverse) vs. dynamic analyzers (sensor)  
   - Depict two image‐build paths: internal builder vs. Docker Engine  
   - Include external dependencies: Docker daemon, Kubernetes API server, container registries  
   - Illustrate command handlers (xray, build, debug, run, lint, registry, vulnerability) as plugins around the Master core  

7. Guidelines for crafting the diagram  
   - Draw distinct boxes for:  
     * CLI Front-End  
     * Master Controller  
     * Sensor Agent (side-car in target container)  
     * Static Analysis Modules  
     * Dynamic Analysis Modules  
     * Image Builder Engines  
     * Docker/K8s Adapters  
     * External systems (Docker daemon, K8s API, Registries)  
   - Use directional arrows to show:  
     * Command flow (User → CLI → Master)  
     * Control calls (Master → Adapters → Runtimes)  
     * Data flow (Sensor → IPC → Master; Static analyzers → Master; Master → Builder → Runtimes)  
   - Color-code or shape-code:  
     * Green boxes for user-facing components (CLI, commands)  
     * Blue for core services (Master, Analyzers, Builders)  
     * Orange for extensions/adapters (Docker API, K8s API)  
     * Gray for external systems (Docker daemon, Registry, K8s cluster)  
   - Label each arrow with the API or protocol: Docker API calls, IPC volume copy, HTTP probes, syscalls via fanotify/ptrace, registry push/pull  
   - Include notes for special flows: HTTP probing, Seccomp/AppArmor generation, interactive prompt  

8. Detail level & completeness  
   - Capture every architectural element (static vs. dynamic analysis, builder paths, runtime adapters)  
   - Show how sensor is deployed and communicates back  
   - Don’t oversimplify: show both internal and external build engines, Docker vs. Kubernetes modes  
   - Keep the diagram readable with clear labels, consistent shapes, and grouped components  

By following this structure you will have a comprehensive, accurate system-design diagram that reflects SlimToolkit’s modular, extensible architecture and how it interacts with container runtimes, performs analysis, and produces optimized artifacts. 
</explanation>
